title: TWU vs UNT: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: Texas Woman's University (TWU) versus University of North Texas Health Science Center (UNT). Also searched as UNT vs TWU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University and the University of North Texas Health Science Center are both public institutions, but they differ significantly in size and location. Texas Woman's University, located in Denton, has an undergraduate enrollment of 8,767 students, whereas the University of North Texas Health Science Center in Fort Worth has a much smaller undergraduate population of 41. Additionally, Texas Woman's University charges an in-state tuition of $8,640, while the University of North Texas Health Science Center does not provide in-state tuition data. These differences highlight the distinct characteristics of each institution.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Texas Woman's University and the University of North Texas Health Science Center differ in their tuition costs and student debt. Texas Woman's University charges an in-state tuition of $8,640 and an out-of-state tuition of $18,480. In contrast, the University of North Texas Health Science Center does not provide specific tuition data for either in-state or out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Texas Woman's University is $19,218, while no median debt information is available for the University of North Texas Health Science Center. These financial figures reflect some of the cost considerations prospective students might evaluate when comparing Texas Woman's University versus the University of North Texas Health Science Center.
